title: Offer the reboot after a channel switch
head: f6f8b911c572
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A wrapper-capable but pre-flag destination updater can cancel a channel switch and falsely report success
leads.consequence: The existing ~/omarchy dev checkout is deliberately not pulled before activation; a checkout at the actual merge-base has the required sudo wrapper but its updater only knows -y. The hardened channel switch now invokes that old updater with --confirmed. It asks Continue with update? again. If the user chooses No (or input cannot answer), none of the updater's snapshot, migrations, hooks or reboot offer run. The old updater exits 0 because the failed confirm is inside an if with no else, so channel-set's ERR trap and recovery message never fire even after the channel has been linked, pacman channel changed and packages swapped, with reboot-required marker left until a later reboot. The same mismatch can arise when switching to a wrapper-capable earlier packaged release. The next explicit update can complete it, but the switch itself reports success. Before the change the -y handoff skipped that second confirm. Check flag capability or choose a compatible fallback before dev mutation and after packaged transaction, and propagate cancellation as an incomplete switch.

leads.summary: Open PR #13444 implements the same handoff with a different flag; its two files cannot be merged without resolving flag compatibility
leads.consequence: #13444 is open, diverged (compare API) and changes the same updater and channel handoff from the same pre-change lines, but names the new flag --skip-confirm rather than --confirmed. Applying its own diff to this head rejects both scripts; three-way merge with actual merge-base has conflict markers in both. GitHub reports #13444 MERGEABLE against its own base, not a guarantee it merges with this head. Taking the flag check from one PR and channel handoff from the other would restore the duplicate confirmation; the updater's prior-version behavior makes a declined question exit 0 and skip the update. Coordinate the alternative PRs or retain one consistent flag across handoff, updater, docs and tests.

leads.summary: The new flag is absent from generated help examples, and the update-process flow still says only -y skips confirmation
leads.consequence: The new args header correctly generates `omarchy update [-y|--confirmed]`, but the adjacent `omarchy:examples` still contains only ordinary update and -y. The CLI router displays those two under Examples, hiding the distinction important to callers trying to preserve interactive reboot, and the update-process flow documents 'confirm unless -y', which is no longer true. Add `omarchy update --confirmed` to examples and document that both -y and --confirmed skip the opening question, but only -y marks unattended.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** `docs/update-process.md` was not updated for the new `--confirmed` flag; no defects were found in the code change itself.

### `docs/update-process.md` does not document `--confirmed`

The pipeline diagram still says `confirm unless -y` (line 128), and the flag notes describe only `-y` (line 161). **Impact:** the reference doc no longer lists every way the confirmation is skipped, and does not say that only `-y` sets `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED` and so suppresses the reboot offer.

**Suggested change:** add `--confirmed` at both places and note that, unlike `-y`, it keeps the reboot offer and the package-conflict handoff interactive.

<details><summary>Optional notes</summary>

**Optional test improvement:** the new check `grep -q '^omarchy-update-restart unattended=$'` matches either restart call (`--services-only` or `--reboot-only`), so a mutation that marks only the reboot phase unattended still passes (reproducer below). **Suggested change:** assert on the last `omarchy-update-restart` line, which is the reboot phase.
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer for the optional test note (mutation survives at f6f8b91)</summary>

The new `--confirmed` check in `test/shell.d/update-sequence-test.sh` looks for any line matching `^omarchy-update-restart unattended=$`. `omarchy-update` calls `omarchy-update-restart` twice (`--services-only`, then `--reboot-only`), and the step stub does not record which phase it is. Only the second call offers the reboot. So a change that marks just the reboot phase unattended still passes.

Mutation applied to `bin/omarchy-update` at f6f8b911:

```diff
@@ -159,5 +159,6 @@
   omarchy-update-stay-awake stop
   update_stay_awake_stopped=1
 
+  [[ ${1:-} != "--confirmed" ]] || export OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=1
   "$OMARCHY_PATH/bin/omarchy-update-restart" --reboot-only
 fi
```

`bash test/shell.d/update-sequence-test.sh` with that mutation (exit 0):

```
ok - an update where every step works runs all of them, in order
ok - -y is what marks an update unattended, not the update itself
ok - --confirmed skips the update question but keeps the reboot offer
ok - a blocked package upgrade stops the update before it migrates
```

A stricter form of the assertion checks the last restart call, which is the reboot phase:

```diff
@@ -97,7 +97,7 @@
 run_update --confirmed </dev/null || fail "an update confirmed by its caller reports a failure"
 diff <(expected_steps) <(steps_run) >"$test_tmp/order" ||
   fail "--confirmed still asks the person to confirm the update" "$(cat "$test_tmp/order")"
-grep -q '^omarchy-update-restart unattended=$' "$test_tmp/steps" ||
+[[ $(grep '^omarchy-update-restart ' "$test_tmp/steps" | tail -n 1) == "omarchy-update-restart unattended=" ]] ||
   fail "--confirmed marks the update unattended, so the reboot offer is skipped"
 pass "--confirmed skips the update question but keeps the reboot offer"
```

With the stricter assertion and the mutation (exit 1):

```
ok - an update where every step works runs all of them, in order
ok - -y is what marks an update unattended, not the update itself
not ok - --confirmed marks the update unattended, so the reboot offer is skipped
```

With the stricter assertion at f6f8b911, unmutated (exit 0):

```
ok - an update where every step works runs all of them, in order
ok - -y is what marks an update unattended, not the update itself
ok - --confirmed skips the update question but keeps the reboot offer
ok - a blocked package upgrade stops the update before it migrates
```
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (sandboxed repository fixtures at f6f8b91):
- A real `omarchy-channel-set stable` → `omarchy-update` → `omarchy-update-restart` chain with a reboot-required marker shows the `gum confirm` reboot prompt at head, never calls `omarchy-update-confirm`, and ends with sudo revoked. At the merge-base it prints the "Run omarchy-system-reboot when ready." hint instead.
- `--confirmed` survives the `script` logging and lock re-execs; `omarchy update --confirmed` and `omarchy up --confirmed` reach `omarchy-update` with that argument.
- `-y` still skips the confirmation and sets `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=1` on both restart phases.
- The new `update-sequence-test.sh` check and the updated `channel-test.sh` expectations pass at head and fail against the merge-base scripts.

**Older destinations:** an updater that already has the no-update sudo wrapper but predates this flag (for example an unpulled `~/omarchy` dev checkout) treats `--confirmed` as an unknown argument and asks "Ready to update?" once, as the PR body says. If that question is declined, `omarchy-channel-set` exits 0 after the refresh and package swap, without migrations or the reboot offer. With `-y` that updater always ran. This path is transitional and user-initiated.

**Package-conflict handoff:** `omarchy-update-system-pkgs-when-conflicted` also reads `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED`, so a package conflict that reaches the update's own package step during a channel switch now re-runs pacman interactively instead of exiting with a hint. This is rare in a switch, since its refresh already ran `pacman -Syyuu --noconfirm` (source reading, not executed). The new code comment intends this; the PR body does not mention it.

**Related PRs:** #13444 (`--skip-confirm`) edits the same lines of `bin/omarchy-update` and `bin/omarchy-channel-set`, so only one of the two can merge as is. #13616 (runs `omarchy-update` without `-y` on a TTY) also targets #13416, but is based on an older `omarchy-channel-set` and currently shows merge conflicts.
</details>
